solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Level 4's trim bathroom parts …

indicators.note: the bathroom word parts, or splits, the edging letters by sitting between them
trim as the edging of something, so only the outside letters of the number word are kept

parts.note: 4 points to the number four, written out as a word
loo is British slang for a toilet or bathroom

explanation.surface: A decorator's note on how the edging from flat 4 is fitted around bathroom sections.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4' refers to the number, not to 4-across: its edge letters F and R are split by LOO. The ellipsis just carries the sentence on into 4-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a storey of a building is a level, as in the third level or floor.

clue.text: Under discussion, much of Cilla's position as a rock singer

indicators.note: under discussion means being spoken about, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: Cilla Black, the Liverpool singer and TV host, said 'a lorra lorra laughs', so her 'much of' is lorra; position is lie

explanation.surface: Talk of the singer Cilla Black's standing as a rock vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black, a 1960s Liverpool singer turned TV presenter, famously said 'a lorra' for 'a lot of'; add 'lie', a position, and say it aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend: the siren of the Rhine sat on a rock and lured boatmen with song.

clue.text: Evoking William III, always last to open the morning press?

parts.note: William III was William of Orange, so something reminiscent of him could be called Orange-esque

indicators.note: the last letter is placed to open up the always word, sitting inside it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A historical newspaper always reporting on William of Orange at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'morning press' suggests newspapers; it is a device for pressing fruit for breakfast juice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a juicer for citrus presses fruit at breakfast time.

clue.text: … directors having nothing to do in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: someone with nothing to do is bored

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1-across: company bosses idle while someone tries out for a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: a company's directors sit together as its governing body, the board.

clue.text: Registering positive, having got some way through course after several strokes

definitions.meaning: in golf scoring a plus figure means more strokes than the standard

definitions.text: having got some way through course after several strokes
definitions.meaning: a golfer partway round who has taken extra shots is behind the standard total

explanation.surface: A golfer partway round reports their score after a few shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf term: a score more than the expected number of strokes, shown as a plus figure.

clue.text: Heatedly protest Spooner's shortened king's time in power

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: the king shortened to his abbreviation K, with the possessive: said as 'Kay's'
a monarch's reign is their time in power

explanation.surface: A monarch's brief reign is cut short by Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kay's reign' with its first sounds swapped is heard as 'raise Cain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to make a loud, angry fuss, from the biblical Cain.

clue.text: A critical time indeed, having seen regular payment leaving bank

indicators.note: the indeed word has seen, or followed, the payment letters, so it comes after

parts.note: DD is short for direct debit, a regular payment from a bank account
ay is an old form of yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A tense moment when a standing order has gone out of the account.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended sense: the Normandy landing day of 1944 now names any decisive moment.

clue.text: Totally reasonable source, even if a solicitor

parts.note: a well is a source of water
though means even if
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor

explanation.surface: A fair-minded source even when that source is a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a British lawyer; here it is someone who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: carefully considered and logical in every detail.

clue.text: Justice — initially what's not done to restrict Salome's originator, rising playwright

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the first word
in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up
the no-no hems in, restricting, the letter from Salome

parts.note: a no-no is something not done

indicators.note: the originator of Salome's name is its first letter

explanation.surface: A judge curbing Oscar Wilde's play Salome, about an up-and-coming dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the S-filled NOSNO round to ONSON, after J.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ben Jonson was an Elizabethan and Jacobean playwright.

clue.text: Something to impress, presented by newspaper as fine material

indicators.note: the thing to impress is presented, or preceded, by the newspaper word, so it comes second

parts.note: a newspaper is an organ, a mouthpiece for news or views
a die is the stamp used to impress a design on coins or metal

explanation.surface: A publicity stunt: a paper shows off something impressive as a fine fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, sheer cotton fabric, the British spelling of organdy.

clue.text: It's chilling, hearing Scotty's confirmation of Vulcan ownership?

indicators.note: hearing tells us to go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Scotty, the Scottish engineer in Star Trek, would say Aye for yes, and the Vulcan is Mr Spock, so the reply to whose it is is 'Aye, Spock's'

explanation.surface: A Star Trek scene: the ship's engineer confirming something belongs to the Vulcan officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose, a Scottish 'Aye, Spock's' run together to suggest the two words of a fridge. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an old word for a refrigerator, the cabinet that keeps food cold.

clue.text: Sticky mud pots going unfired?

indicators.note: to pot is to put into a pot, so the mud word holds the other letters

parts.note: clay is a heavy sticky soil, a kind of mud

indicators.note: with the fire, its glowing heart, taken out, only the shell of the word going is left

explanation.surface: A potter's complaint: muddy clay pots still waiting for the kiln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfired' reads as unbaked pottery, but it strips the heart of 'going', leaving its two outer letters. 'pots' means the mud word holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: claggy is a northern British dialect word for clinging and sticky, especially of mud.

clue.text: Lord's lower in estimation, having no matches

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm; the 's is read as 'is', joining it to what follows
less, as in thought less of, means lower in estimation

explanation.surface: A nobleman has fallen in people's regard because he has been unmatched.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something without equal has nothing to rival it.

clue.text: He's one of the few who knows how Rosie likes to be kept, allegedly?

definitions.text: one of the few who knows

indicators.note: allegedly means as it is said, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.words: how Rosie likes to be kept
parts.note: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's memoir of a Gloucestershire boyhood, so Rosie is kept in cider

explanation.surface: A gossip claiming to know how a woman called Rosie likes to be treated.
explanation.walkthrough: Cider with Rosie is a famous English memoir by Laurie Lee, so Rosie is kept 'in cider'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an insider is someone within a group with access to private information.

clue.text: A little coffee set aside to be drunk with the last of cream

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling, so the letters are mixed up
the last of picks the final letter

explanation.surface: Coffee put by to be drunk later, with the dregs of the cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like the coffee being drunk; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a demitasse is a small cup of strong black coffee, French for half-cup.

clue.text: Conveniently near English city and Bishop goes AWOL

indicators.note: to go AWOL is to be absent without leave, so the bishop's letter is missing

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, south-west England
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric absconds from a cathedral city that is handy for travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something close by, ready to use, is near to one's reach.

clue.text: Account to use when talking through 'very little money'? There's nothing in it!

indicators.note: the account letters run through, inside, the outer pair

parts.note: little points to the short form, M for money

indicators.note: when talking says the words are taken as spoken

parts.note: 'to use' said aloud sounds like 'two Us', written as a pair of the letter U

explanation.surface: A bank customer told which account to use for a near-empty balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when talking' turns 'to use' into 'two Us', UU; with AC it goes 'through' V and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a vacuum is a space with no matter in it at all.

clue.text: Check out presence at wine-drinkers' heaven under a counter

indicators.note: in a down clue the god goes under the a
out means the check letters are taken away

parts.note: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine, the presiding presence for drinkers
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Checking up on who is behind a bar in drinkers' paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a bar; here it is a device for counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an abacus is a frame of beads used for counting.

clue.text: Cut in order to guarantee tip off

indicators.note: the tip, the first letter, comes off the guarantee word

parts.note: to ensure something is to guarantee it

explanation.surface: An informant must be silenced to keep a deal safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head, a haircut.

clue.text: See if the cap fits fool (or at least attempt to)?

definitions.meaning: trying on a hat to check the size
to attempt to deceive someone, to chance your arm

explanation.surface: Try on a hat to see if it fits, or attempt to trick someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom with two senses: test clothing, or try to get away with a deception.

clue.text: Glimpse old governor cutting West-East, then heading North

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means read upwards
the governor cuts into the West-East letters

parts.note: Mae West, the film star, gives Mae; East is E
a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A former governor slicing across a map from west to east and then going north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is Mae West, the film actress, not a direction; MAE BEY E is read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Old word: an eyebeam is a glance, a beam of sight from the eye.

clue.text: Wall-pictures to view, recordings to hear

parts.note: tapes are audio or video recordings
a judge hears a case, which is to try it

explanation.surface: Things to look at hanging up, and recordings to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: woven hangings depicting scenes are hung on walls as pictures.

clue.text: Top producer of #fruit?

indicators.note: top as a verb, to cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the # symbol is produced by the hash key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A hashtag about the best fruit grower.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical term: the winged seed of the ash tree is called a key.

clue.text: A girl's bottom's been pinched, I regret to say

indicators.note: the bottom, last letter, of the girl word has been pinched, stolen

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that a young woman has been groped.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection: an expression of sorrow or regret.

clue.text: Division of Apple's most powerful men

definitions.meaning: the Big Apple is New York, and one of its five boroughs is named after a royal consort
in chess the most powerful pieces, or men, are the ones beside each king

explanation.surface: Apple's corporate division where the bosses with the most power sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple' looks like the tech company; with the capital it is the Big Apple, New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Double meaning: a New York borough, and the strongest chess pieces.

clue.text: Briefly engaged cutting green-blue cloth

indicators.note: the engaged phrase cuts into the colour word

parts.note: teal is a greenish-blue colour

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an engaged couple is going to wed

explanation.surface: A couple, briefly engaged, cutting up a blue-green fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' is the phrase 'to wed', and 'Briefly' drops its final letter before 'cutting' puts the rest inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: a tea towel is a cloth for drying washed dishes.

clue.text: Miserable smidgeon taken from spending-money? …

indicators.note: miserable suggests something wretched and reduced, so the letters of smidgeon are jumbled before they are removed

explanation.surface: A tiny sum skimmed off pocket money is a meagre amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' says the letters of SMIDGEON are removed from SPENDINGMONEY; the five left over make the answer. Read whole, the clue describes a tiny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a penny is the smallest British coin, a miserably small amount.

clue.text: … sons stop press

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons
to tamp is to plug or stop up a hole, as when packing a blasting charge

explanation.surface: Continuing from 25-across: boys halt the printing presses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stamp is to press down hard, as with a foot or a seal.
